status: prospective before implementation, no new strength games
hypothesis: Native opening inference already computes per-piece mobile-rank probabilities but discards them. Replacing only exchangeable mobile capture gain with the same posterior's per-piece expectation can improve attack choice without another rollout or model.
distinction: C11 uses count/joint Flag-Bomb priors with exchangeable mobile ranks in the Teacher. This tests source-template mobile identities in the stronger native-template policy, with all Flag/Bomb Q12 values preserved exactly. It does not add a new Flag prior, danger correction or search horizon.
algorithm: For hidden-target captures, retain native quantized Flag/Bomb/mobile masses and public piece worths. Replace the mobile conditional expected gain from public remaining rank counts by the target's conditional mobile expectation from the existing source-template posterior. Native signed truncation and the near-own-Flag conditional capture bonus must be reconstructed exactly. Public captures and quiet moves keep their scores; select from one native scored move search and correct actual-choice history on override. No additional random draws.
gates: Exact zero correction for exchangeable mobile posterior
Full public inventory and own-Flag bonus agreement with native source
Portable runtime and no-op decision/history parity
Fresh immutable policy and paired DOS/honest screens
risk: Per-piece mobile posterior can be confidently wrong on procedural armies; correction of capture gain alone leaves native danger and persistent routes exchangeable. Any success is a playing-strength result for that partial bridge, not full posterior planning.
target: Desktop prototype; no CX16 fit claim. First measure a clear strategic effect before considering banked representation.
comparison: Unchanged student-template-flag-bomb-v1-normal; same deployments, Flag/Bomb packets, source template model, RNG and one native search. Fresh source-seeded cohorts only, no tuning on validation results.
